findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: It was observed that no employees present during today’s inspection had completed a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/CFPM) course. A CFM should be present at all times during which food is being prepared or handled. The presence of a CFM is able to oversee proper employee hygiene, food handling practices, safe holding temperatures, and overall reduces the risk of food-borne illness. Ensure a CFM is present on staff during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.[C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to operate the faucet handles after completing the handwashing process. Be sure to educate employees on proper handwashing procedures. After washing hands, make sure to use a barrier to operate faucet handles to prevent contaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.comment:

2) Biofilm at the soda gun holder on the North side of the bar. CORRECTED- the space was wiped with a sanitizer cloth. 
Ensure all food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:

CORRECTED- All out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Several foods (salsa, lettuce, sour cream, and southwest ranch) were 45F or below and were moved to a functioning cooler.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

NOTE: Sprayer sink and drain board are both loose and not sealed to the wall. A decent size gap would be present if caulk were to be removed. The gap would allow for cleaning between the equipment and the wall if facility wishes to do away with caulk. For ease in cleaning another alternative would be installation of a stainless steel backslash panel that would provide a more secure seal.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for potential cross contamination, handwashing, and glove use. An employee was observed using a handwashing sink for a task unrelated to handwashing, and soap was not available at the bar handwashing sink. Kitchen dish machine was also in need of service as hot water sanitizing rinse entering at the manifold was above the maximum allowed temperature. Active managerial controls were discussed. Corrective actions and active managerial controls will be revisited at the re-inspection on 9/27/22.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Cook washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to drying hands. GM educated cook on proper technique. Ensure all staff are properly washing hands between tasks. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:

Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Salad plates were observed in pans soiled with food debris in the bottom right drawer of the southwest cooler on the make line. One plate was inverted allowing the food contact surfaces to be in direct contact with the soiled pan. Pan and salad plates were removed from the cooler to be cleaned and sanitized.

Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Freshly dispensed sanitizer solutions in sani-buckets were almost 0ppm quat with very little color change to test strips. Both instant change (inspector) and litmus paper (facility) test strips were used. Management indicated the dispenser doesn’t consistently work and one of the dish washers manually adds the concentrated product at the 3 part sink prior to adding quat solution from the dispenser to get the correct concentration. This practice has occurred for ~2 weeks now. The front cover of the dispenser was loose and hanging down toward the 3 part sink. Call for service was made during inspection. In the meantime, quat solutions for sanitizer-buckets were mixed manually to provide solutions at 400ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 1. Pan of bacon aioli in the walk-in cooler had a day dot showing the prep date of 3/31. Discard date per the label was 4/3 per company requirement. Thursday 4/7 was the last day for use per the date marking requirement of the food code. Product was discarded during inspection.
2. Container of sautéed onions was observed in the walk-in cooler without a date mark. Manager noted the product was likely leftover from the previous evening and should not have been kept. Sautéed onions were discarded.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Hot Shot spray pesticide was observed under the counter at the south end of the bar. Manager was advised on the use of pesticides in the facility, and product was removed from the bar. Residential use products are not intended for use in a food service establishment. Ensure labeling indicates products may be used in a food service establishment and work with PCO to determine available products. 
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions state that use is allowed in a food establishment.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 1. Dozens of fruit flies were observed at the south end of the bar underneath counters and by the paper towel dispenser at the handwashing sink. PCO arrived for monthly service and sprayed to eliminate active flies under counters near drains at the bar. PCO advised management the floor drains need to be thoroughly cleaned before treatment of drains can occur. Drains are believed to be the main source of the issue.
2. Facility has current rodent activity. Staff noted seeing at least one mouse in the bar area in the last few days and sometimes seeing mice around the kitchen handwashing sinks in the early morning hours upon arriving to work and/or in the evening at closing time. Rodent trap was observed with a half dozen dead mice in the corner by the media box at the north end of the bar. PCO scanned the trap and noted it was not on the current service rotation, which means someone moved the trap from its original location resulting in the trap being eliminated from the service rotation. Corner where trap was located has an entry point that needs to be sealed. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Final rinse surface temperature after over a half dozen full ware washing cycles was observed below 160F. Inspector and facility dish temp testers indicated surface temperatures of 153F and 156F respectively. Those surface temperatures remained after a few additional ware washing cycles. Call for service was made, and technician arrived for service during inspection. After adjusting the rinse setting, the surface temperature was observed at 163F.
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be properly sanitized in hot water mechanical operations cycled through properly functioning equipment and achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F a measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.112 Dish machine rinse gauge was not working consistently. The final rinse temperature coming in at the manifold went from 180F down to 170F and slightly below prior to moving back up to around 170F during rinse cycles. Manager ran an additional cycle later and noted the gauge got up to about 178F. A call for service was made, and technician arrived for service during inspection. The rinse setting was adjusted slightly and allowed for a consistent rinse temperature at the manifold remaining at 180F-190F.
Except as specified in ¶ (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F or less than 180F.
